mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous year - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 10% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not statistically significant at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% while personal income (PAYEMS) grows below 1% signals a shift from spending to saving, implying lower consumer demand and reduced corporate sales, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND PAYEMS monthly change < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which raises wage growth and input costs, ultimately compressing margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not significant at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900,000 units for six consecutive months signals a deepening housing market contraction, which reduces construction-related economic activity and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at the 10% level.
